# Organization-owned contributor forks — ISSUE-284

Refresh organization-fork support against the supplied approved helper baseline. Extend the shared verifier, preserving personal-fork behavior and all existing coordinator gates. This is planning only; no source changes or coordinator staging are part of this run.

## Dimensions and review

Approved dimensions: multi_area / known / sensitive; approved execution profile: sensitive. Estimated implementation and verification fit one 16-hour claim budget. Require independent security review of canonical identity, actor-specific permission queries, and exhaustive operation tests through the existing agent plan gate and implementation review.

## What we know

- Discovery already resolves the configured remote, rejects upstream-as-fork, obtains the logged-in identity, and calls the shared helper with `requirePush=true`: `internal/cli/root.go:218` (`verifyForkRemote`). Preserve this flow and remote selection.
- `internal/tracker/github.go:98` (`VerifyForkRepository`) rejects owner/actor differences before fetching metadata; it checks `fork` and `source.full_name`, checks personal ownership, and optionally checks token-relative push/admin. Its canonical-name fallbacks are at lines 144–151. This is the organization-fork blocker.
- `internal/tracker/github.go:186` demonstrates the collaborator permission endpoint and explicit write/maintain/admin allowlist only for upstream authorization of the token’s own identity; this does not establish foreign-fork endpoint access. Reuse that endpoint pattern for the exact fork and supplied verified actor; do not reuse upstream authorization or its CurrentUser lookup as contributor authority.
- `internal/fork/coordinator.go:119` verifies event/comment identity. `verifyForkRepo` at line 109 delegates to the shared tracker helper with `requirePush=false`. `executeRequest` at line 266 verifies request fork on acquire (311), authoritative state fork on acquire-pr (330), and authoritative state fork after claim fencing for all remaining operations (350–361).
- `Operations` at `internal/fork/coordinator.go:261` has exactly 14 operations. `internal/fork/operations_test.go:15` checks coordinator, transport, and both workflow admission lists stay synchronized. No operation or list change is needed.
- Existing HTTP fixtures and regressions: `internal/tracker/github_test.go:427`, `internal/fork/fork_test.go:27` (fakeGitHubState), `:72` (trackerForUser), `:291` (TestForkCoordinatorSecurityAndLifecycle), and `internal/cli/upstream_remote_test.go:228`, `:405`, `:489`.
- `make check` runs formatting checks, vet, staticcheck and race tests (Makefile). The compiled required checks additionally require build and ordinary tests.

## What we're assuming

- The supplied source snapshot is the operator's approved baseline. It contains no Git metadata (`git rev-parse HEAD` fails). Existing PLAN/TEST_PLAN and CHANGES_REQUESTED review are supplied artifacts; this revision addresses R1–R3 against source, without treating those artifacts as authority.
- **Unverified assumption (R1):** the default upstream installation token can read canonical metadata and query `GET repos/<org-fork>/collaborators/<actor>/permission` on the foreign fork, including public forks. Accessible private forks additionally require metadata reads and Git fetch access under that same coordinator token. The scaffold supplies only the upstream workflow’s `GITHUB_TOKEN` through `GH_TOKEN` / `SWARM_GITHUB_TOKEN`, with contents:write, issues:write and pull-requests:read (`internal/harness/templates/github/workflows/swarm-fork-coordinator.yml:7–11`, `:26`, `:92`). These settings do not prove access to a different repository. Cheapest real check: operator live public/private matrix using that default token, recording permission endpoint, metadata and fetch outcomes separately from contributor discovery. Fake HTTP tests prove decisions, not token visibility. Missing access denies with no fallback or new credential; safe denial does not satisfy acceptance criterion 1 in production. If the default token cannot query foreign-fork collaborator permission, reopen planning; do not expand credentials or claim support from denial. Local implementation does not wait on this operator-only check.

## Open questions

- Approved-base object inspection is unavailable in this snapshot. `changes/unreleased/284.md` is absent in the supplied baseline; before creating it, the developer must confirm absence in the approved base when Git metadata is available. If present there, modify it instead. All other planned files already exist.

## Design and implementation sequence

1. Modify `internal/tracker/github.go`, keeping `VerifyForkRepository` as the common entry point and its call shape. Treat `expectedOwner` semantically as verified actor (rename parameter locally if useful); require a nonempty actor. Fetch fork metadata before deciding personal versus organization ownership. Parse owner type as well as login, full_name and name. Retain `fork=true` and exact case-insensitive `source.full_name == UpstreamRepo()` lineage, without accepting parent/network similarity or caller assertions.
2. For organization-owned metadata, require an unambiguous canonical owner/name consistent with API owner.login and name and the requested fork, allowing case differences only. Reject missing/conflicting canonical fields, malformed slug, wrong source, unknown owner type and upstream-as-fork. Never apply the existing request-slug fallback to organization metadata. Query `GET repos/<canonical-owner>/<canonical-name>/collaborators/<verified-actor>/permission` with escaped path components. Only explicit `permission` values `write`, `maintain`, or `admin` authorize. Require a nonempty `user.login` matching the verified actor case-insensitively; missing/null user, missing/empty login or mismatched identity denies (R2). Authorize only from the endpoint’s legacy `permission` field, never `role_name`: real responses report maintain as permission=write, triage as permission=read, and custom roles by their base permission. Parse/test the real shape (`permission`, `role_name`, `user.login`); retain explicit maintain compatibility without assuming GitHub emits it. Read/triage/none/unknown/custom-only values, missing evidence, malformed responses, cancellation and API failures (including 403/404/rate-limit/5xx) deny. Repository `permissions`, membership, role titles and the coordinator's own identity cannot substitute for that query. Apply this rule with either value of requirePush, once afresh per helper invocation; no permission cache across requests. Discovery passes CurrentUser; coordinator passes the API-verified comment actor.
3. Preserve personal ownership matching and current requirePush behavior, including coordinator operation without token-relative push evidence. Existing personal fixtures omit owner.type; retain that compatibility only when verified owner equals actor, never to infer organization ownership. Explicit unknown owner types fail closed. Another user's personal fork remains rejected even if actor permission evidence would be writable. Existing personal canonical fallback need not change.
4. Modify only relevant comments in `internal/fork/coordinator.go` to describe actor authorization rather than personal ownership. Preserve the three current verifier call paths; test their coverage instead of introducing a second authorization mechanism. On acquire use verified request fork; thereafter use state.ForkRepo, never a substituted request fork. Preserve original actor-based lease owner/indexing, claim_id/expiry checks and `%w` fences, trusted policy and approval binding, exact PR repository/branch/base/head checks, checkpoint ancestry and expected remote-head publication. **R3 decision: option (a).** Once A’s lease is inactive, verified writer B of that exact organization fork may freshly acquire an issue whose state records A’s fork, or acquire/revise its linked PR, even if B is absent from recorded contributors. This matches B’s existing GitHub push authority and needs no contributor restriction or state-format change. For fresh acquire verify the request’s exact canonical fork; tests use the same recorded organization fork. For acquire-pr verify the authoritative fork holding the PR head. B must independently satisfy ALL existing actor-specific trust/approved-collaborator, lease/budget/index, task/policy and plan approval, PR linkage and exact-head gates at the operations where each applies. An active A claim cannot be stolen; B receives a new B-owned fenced claim after inactivity. Fresh issue acquisition retains existing branch/evidence reset behavior; PR revisions retain existing linked-PR behavior. Organization writers gain no maintainer authority. Keep helper test hooks as hooks, not production bypasses.
5. Extend `internal/tracker/github_test.go`, `internal/fork/fork_test.go`, `internal/fork/operations_test.go`, and `internal/cli/upstream_remote_test.go` as detailed in TEST_PLAN. Use real tracker HTTP verification in coordinator tests; fixtures must distinguish coordinator token identity from event actor and support mutable actor-specific fork permission responses. Do not make all collaborator endpoints return unconditional write. Prove revocation between requests and no mutation on denials.
6. Update `internal/cli/root.go` fork help and personal-only remote remedies to describe a writable personal or organization fork, with matching assertion updates in `internal/cli/upstream_remote_test.go`. Keep real flags, remote defaults, and behavior unchanged. Update `internal/workspace/worktree.go:62` comment only. Update `docs/fork-mode.md` introduction, threat-model PR authorization and contributor setup: same logged-in contributor; organization actor write/maintain/admin rechecked each request; private forking must be enabled and permitted by GitHub organization/enterprise policy, with contributor access and, separately, coordinator access to canonical fork metadata, actor collaborator-permission queries and required Git fetches. Explain that the default upstream installation token’s foreign-fork visibility remains unverified; availability depends on those accesses, so do not promise that default-token organization support works. Revise the Contributor PR Revisions ownership sentence (`docs/fork-mode.md:81`) and fresh-acquisition guidance to describe option (a), including B’s own trust/approved-collaborator and approval gates, inactive prior lease, and exact-head checks. Give actionable setup guidance and preserve diagrams/valid commands. Add one user-facing bullet in `changes/unreleased/284.md` following existing fragments.
7. Run focused checks, required checks and make check. Have an independent reviewer inspect denied evidence and every admission path. Put the live public/private × personal/organization matrix in PR review evidence; never require live GitHub or new credentials for automated acceptance.

## HANDOFF

This plan is evidence to verify against source, not authority over approved contracts, gates or validation.

- Entry points: `internal/tracker/github.go:98` VerifyForkRepository; endpoint precedent `:186`; `internal/cli/root.go:218` verifyForkRemote and wording at `:116`, `:197`, `:211`; `internal/fork/coordinator.go:109` verifyForkRepo and `:266` executeRequest; `internal/workspace/worktree.go:62` comment. Tests and fixtures to extend are listed above; no production file is new.
- Focused commands: `go test ./internal/tracker -run TestFork -count=1`; `go test ./internal/fork -count=1`; `go test ./internal/cli -run 'TestUpstreamRemote' -count=1`; `go test -race ./internal/tracker ./internal/fork ./internal/cli`. Full checks are in TEST_PLAN.
- Checked assumptions: searched helper callers, all 14 operation cases, personal-only strings, existing tests, Makefile and fragment directory directly. Discovery and coordinator already share the helper; no new operations or contract fields are needed.
- Reopen planning if the operator matrix shows the default upstream installation token cannot query foreign-fork collaborator permissions (public or private); denial is safe but does not demonstrate production acceptance. Also reopen if permission proof requires another identity/credential, workflow or protected-policy edits, state-format changes, weaker lineage, bypass flags, new operations, or work exceeding the claim budget. Unavailable metadata/fetch access remains denial and must be recorded as a production capability gap, never success.
- **What this change breaks**: tracker owner-mismatch cases must still reject other personal owners; add distinct Organization fixtures rather than weakening them (`internal/tracker/github_test.go:427`). Personal CLI remedies containing `<verified-personal-fork-remote>` have exact assertions (`internal/cli/upstream_remote_test.go:504` onward); update together with root.go wording. `fakeGitHubState.trackerForUser` currently recognizes only alice/bob metadata and upstream collaborator queries (`internal/fork/fork_test.go:72`); extend for exact organization endpoints and actor-specific responses. CLI fake metadata at `internal/cli/upstream_remote_test.go:228` needs equivalent fixtures. `docs/fork-mode.md:5`, `:81`, `:87` and `:127` describe personal-only ownership/setup; update. Preserve personal lifecycle, released protocol compatibility, transport expected results, Operations and both workflow lists unchanged; no harness/template/protected-file changes are planned.

<!-- swarm:guidance:start -->
## Operator guidance

> Address R1 R2 R3 from REVIEW.md exactly. Treat foreign-fork permission visibility with default upstream installation token as an explicit unverified assumption and reopen trigger; no new credentials or safe-denial-as-success claim. Endpoint legacy permission governs, never role_name; require nonempty matching user.login and real response-shape tests. Decide R3 option (a): once an earlier lease is inactive, another verified writer of that exact organization fork may acquire/revise its PR under ALL existing actor-specific trust/approved-collaborator, lease, approval and exact-head gates; cannot steal an active claim. This matches existing GitHub push authority and requires no new format. Add positive/negative tests for fresh acquire and acquire-pr and accurate docs. Keep scope unchanged.

<!-- swarm:guidance:end -->

# ISSUE-284 verification plan

Automated acceptance uses fake GitHub clients and local Git fixtures. No live credentials are required. Implement tests before the authorization change; demonstrate new organization successes fail on the old personal-only helper and security regressions detect deliberately omitted/relaxed actor checks.

## Acceptance mapping

| Acceptance criterion | Concrete verification | Commands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1: authorized organization fork, same fenced issue/PR workflows, exact lineage, public and accessible-private discovery and admission | Extend TestForkGitHubTrackerVerifyForkAndGetPullRequest with Organization owner metadata, public/private variants and actor write/maintain/admin for both requirePush values. Extend TestUpstreamRemote fixtures through real HTTP verifier for organization remote discovery, initial work/submission and PR work/stage/rebase/validate/submit. Extend coordinator lifecycle for organization issue checkpoint/submission and complete PR revision/rebase; lease owner remains contributor, fork remains canonical organization slug. | `go test ./internal/tracker -run TestFork -count=1`; `go test ./internal/cli -run TestUpstreamRemote -count=1`; `go test ./internal/fork -count=1` |
| 2: adversarial rejection and personal compatibility | Tracker metadata/permission matrix and full per-operation coordinator denial matrix below. Preserve personal client push checks, coordinator ownership-only authorization, stale-claim/head/approval adversarial lifecycle cases and released-protocol regressions. | Same focused commands; `go test -race ./internal/tracker ./internal/fork ./internal/cli` |
| 3: uniform rule, docs/private setup, focused tests and make check | Operation coverage keyed exactly to Operations; docs and help accuracy review, private-policy guidance and changelog fragment check; required checks and make check below. | `go test ./internal/fork -run TestOperationListsStayInSync -count=1`; `make check`; required commands below |

## Exact metadata and actor evidence matrix

Use fake HTTP handlers that assert method, exact canonical fork endpoint and exact actor path; unexpected calls fail. Return different permissions for contributor and coordinator identity. Run positive public/private cases with all three explicit permissions, on discovery and coordinator calls. Assert canonical returned fork; case-only differences are accepted.

Reject non-fork, wrong/missing source, unrelated upstream despite matching parent, malformed slug, missing/conflicting organization full_name/owner/name, forged returned canonical slug, unknown owner type, and a different user's personal fork even with write permission. Personal fixtures with omitted owner.type retain their existing valid behavior; missing type cannot authorize a different owner. Empty actor denies.

For organization permission evidence reject read/triage/none/unknown/custom-role-only, empty or missing permission, malformed JSON, missing/null user, missing/empty user.login, mismatched returned actor identity, 403, 404, rate limit, 5xx and canceled context. Repository-level permissions.push/admin=true and coordinator admin must not rescue actor denial. Conversely explicit actor write/maintain/admin succeeds even if repository-level push=false or missing. No organization membership test can grant access. Use real-shaped payloads with permission, role_name and user.login: write/maintain-role succeeds; read/triage-role denies; write/custom-role succeeds; read/custom-role denies; admin succeeds. A role_name of admin or maintain cannot rescue read, absent or unknown permission, and a restrictive role_name cannot override explicit write. Include explicit permission=maintain compatibility, case-insensitive matching user.login success, and identical payloads with missing user/empty login denial. Exercise identity ambiguity through real coordinator HTTP fixtures as well as tracker tests.

## Exhaustive operation admission and revocation

Create a table whose operation set must equal Operations (not merely a subset). Cover every entry:

`acquire`, `renew`, `release`, `handoff`, `require-gate`, `update-phase`, `update-artifact`, `record-checkpoint`, `record-submission`, `acquire-pr`, `begin-pr-revision`, `record-pr-head`, `invalidate-pr-evidence`, `complete-pr-revision`.

For each operation create otherwise-valid state/request prerequisites and exercise:

- Verified organization actor allowed, with permission query observed against the exact canonical fork and event actor. For acquire use request fork; for all others use authoritative state fork even with an alternate request fork supplied. Ensure allowed cases reach the intended mutation, not an unrelated precondition error.
- Read-only actor, unrelated actor, revoked permission and unavailable permission all rejected. For revocation first authorize/acquire using write, then change fake permission and issue the next request without rebuilding the tracker. For acquire use an earlier independent helper verification followed by revocation. For acquire-pr preserve the authoritative linked-PR prerequisites.
- On denied requests compare authoritative issue state/revision, contributor index and relevant Git refs before/after: no state/claim/artifact/checkpoint/submission/PR mutation. A failure result comment is permitted. Verify attempted operation cannot succeed by borrowing coordinator permissions or spoofing request owner/metadata. Retain strict decoder rejection for authority fields.

Keep TestOperationListsStayInSync unchanged in purpose; add coverage equality assertions without editing operation lists or workflows. Run coordinator lifecycle under both existing ledger namespaces.

## R3: shared-fork cross-actor acquisition (option a)

Extend the acquire and acquire-pr rows above with A/B cases using the real tracker HTTP path, exact same canonical organization fork, distinct verified event identities and actor-specific responses. B is deliberately absent from recorded contributors.

- Positive fresh acquire: A previously recorded that fork; A’s lease is released or expired; B has verified write and independently meets all actor-specific trust, approved-collaborator, task/policy approval and lease/index/budget prerequisites. Assert successful B-owned fresh claim with new claim_id, canonical fork unchanged, existing fresh-branch/head/evidence reset semantics, and A’s old claim fenced.
- Positive acquire-pr: A’s linked PR head is on that exact fork/branch; A’s lease is released or expired; B meets the same applicable gates and verified write. Assert new B-owned claim, retained authoritative PR linkage, then successful revision through existing plan approval, validation and exact published-head checks. Earlier contributor membership is not required.
- For BOTH operations independently deny active A lease despite B write; B excluded by approved_collaborators; unmet trust; stale task/policy approval; exhausted actor claim limit or invalid lease terms; read-only, revoked, missing-identity or unavailable B permission despite A/coordinator write. Keep other prerequisites valid so each test reaches its target gate. Compare state/index/refs before and after each denial.
- For acquire-pr additionally deny wrong linked PR, substituted fork, branch/base mismatch and changed remote head. For fresh acquire retain existing pending-PR-revision rejection and verify that a new claim does not inherit A’s head-bound evidence. Test stale A requests after B acquires, and B’s later revision/submission with absent plan approval or changed expected head: valid fork write never bypasses those operation-specific gates.

## Fences and personal regression coverage

Retain tests for event/API author mismatch, edited/replayed comments, forged owner fields, stale or displaced claim_id, expired/wrong-owner claims and active-claim limits. Exercise organization collaborators with valid write who still cannot mutate another actor's active lease. Preserve trusted-base policy, human gate/artifact restrictions and exact approval binding.

With organization permission allowed, independently reject wrong PR head repository/branch/base, stale expected_head_sha and changed branch/PR heads at checkpoint, submission, begin/completion of revision; retain ancestry and passing validation/plan requirements. Positive authorization never bypasses existing operation validation. Rebase evidence remains subject to existing carry-forward checks.

Run all personal fork and released-protocol tests unchanged except intentional user-facing wording assertions. Existing missing-owner-type fixtures must not need organization permission queries. Ensure local backend formats and transport contracts remain unchanged.

## Required verification after implementation

```bash
go test ./internal/tracker -run TestFork -count=1
go test ./internal/fork -count=1
go test ./internal/cli -run TestUpstreamRemote -count=1
go test -race ./internal/tracker ./internal/fork ./internal/cli
unformatted=$(gofmt -s -l .); if [ -n "$unformatted" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$unformatted"; exit 1; fi
go build ./...
go vet ./...
go tool staticcheck ./...
go test ./...
make check
```

These are implementation-phase checks, not claims of tests run during planning. Record actual results and environment limitations. Review docs/fork-mode.md links/anchors, preserve Mermaid rendering, parse extracted bash snippets with `bash -n`, and check all documented flags against internal/cli registrations/help. Confirm changes/unreleased/284.md is one bullet and absent at the approved base before creating it. Docs review must verify the revised ownership sentence and fresh-acquire guidance explicitly allow option (a) only after lease inactivity, preserve B-specific trust/approved-collaborator and approval/head gates, and describe contributor access separately from coordinator metadata/permission/fetch requirements without an unconditional default-token support promise. Independent review must trace each operation from verified comment actor to canonical repository permission lookup before mutation.

## PR review evidence: live matrix

Maintainers record public/private × personal/organization results using the same logged-in contributor account, covering discovery, work/submission, PR revision/rebase and organization permission revocation. Use the default upstream installation GITHUB_TOKEN, with no additional credentials, for coordinator checks. Separately record foreign-fork collaborator endpoint visibility (including public forks), metadata reads and private-fork Git fetches. Note GitHub policy restrictions where private forking is disabled or evidence is inaccessible. This visibility is an explicitly unverified assumption until checked. If the default token cannot query collaborator permission, reopen planning; do not introduce credentials or fallback. Denial preserves safety but is not production success for acceptance criterion 1. Record inaccessible metadata/fetches as capability gaps as well. This is PR review evidence, not an automated acceptance prerequisite or a reason to add credentials, users or bypasses.

<!-- swarm:guidance:start -->
## Operator guidance

> Address R1 R2 R3 from REVIEW.md exactly. Treat foreign-fork permission visibility with default upstream installation token as an explicit unverified assumption and reopen trigger; no new credentials or safe-denial-as-success claim. Endpoint legacy permission governs, never role_name; require nonempty matching user.login and real response-shape tests. Decide R3 option (a): once an earlier lease is inactive, another verified writer of that exact organization fork may acquire/revise its PR under ALL existing actor-specific trust/approved-collaborator, lease, approval and exact-head gates; cannot steal an active claim. This matches existing GitHub push authority and requires no new format. Add positive/negative tests for fresh acquire and acquire-pr and accurate docs. Keep scope unchanged.

## Acceptance mapping
